target: Q-Explorer (QMS RPV CH) prototype — http://127.0.0.1:8099/index.html · Round 1: create & manage an evaluation

checked.item: real Chromium (Playwright, /usr/bin/chromium-browser, headless, 1440x900) — DOM-order inventory of interactive elements per zone, then full Tab cycles with document.activeElement + computed outline/box-shadow readback. State map records no focus behaviour, so all focus evidence is browser-observed.

Tab walk, 14 stops: topbar nav ×5 → lang select → Log out → email → password → Anmelden → Passwort vergessen? → Impressum/Dokumente/Kontaktdaten. All reachable, all show a visible focus ring (outline auto 1–3px).
login-email / login-password — no <label>, no aria-label; both carry a placeholder, so an accessible name exists (not reported)

focus on open / containment / return on Escape — role=dialog + aria-modal=true are present, BUT focus stays on the trigger after Enter, 7 subsequent Tabs all land OUTSIDE the modal (Documents → Support → Contact → New Evaluation → search → both filter selects), and Escape closes it leaving focus on a background filter select, not the trigger. Real defect, dropped for the 4-finding cap.

full Tab cycle to wrap — 53 stops, 18 unique: topbar ×5, lang, Log out, 4 util-links, New Evaluation, search, 2 filter selects, then only Anzeigen + delete row buttons. Focus ring visible at every stop.
sidebar nav-item ×3 (Evaluations / New Evaluation / Scheduled Reports) — DIVs with onclick, no tabindex, no role; never focused in the 53-stop cycle

group-header accordion ×6 — DIVs with onclick, no tabindex, no role; never focused in the 53-stop cycle, so collapsing/expanding a report-type group is mouse-only. Rows are expanded by default so the task survives; dropped for the cap.

'Anzeigen' and 'delete' row buttons — accessible name is 'Anzeigen' / 'delete' with no row context; across 28 rows a screen-reader user hears 14 identical 'delete' buttons with no idea which evaluation. Dropped for the cap.
In-Progress row delete button — pointer-events:none + opacity .35, no disabled attribute, no aria-disabled, tabIndex 0. Interrogated by keyboard: see A11Y-4.

reports-status-filter / reports-period-filter / topbar-lang-select — three <select>s with no <label>, no aria-label, no title, no placeholder: accessible name is empty, a screen reader announces only the current value ('All', 'EN'). Real defect, dropped for the cap.
aria-live / role=status / role=alert regions — ZERO in the entire document, so the toasts ('Evaluation deleted', 'Evaluation started — running now') are never announced. Dropped for the cap.
table semantics — 13 <table>s with 148 real <th> cells (good), though 0 of them carry scope=
6 .type-card elements — DIVs, onclick, no role, tabIndex -1; full Tab cycle of the screen produces zero content stops: see A11Y-1
Tab walk — Back, 6 preset buttons (Last 7 Days…Custom), 7 day-of-week buttons (Mon…Sun), name input, Next: all real <button>/<input>, all reachable, focus ring visible. Step 1 is keyboard-complete.
preset + day-of-week buttons — selected state carried by class 'active' only, no aria-pressed, so a screen reader cannot hear which period or which days are chosen. Dropped for the cap.
6 .custom-select-trigger panels (rpv / mode / canton / tu / lines / stops) — DIVs, no tabindex, no role, no aria-expanded, no aria-haspopup: see A11Y-2
Tab walk of the whole step — topbar ×5, lang, Log out, 4 util-links, Back, Back, Next. Eleven of the fourteen stops are chrome; not one filter control appears.

Tab walk after reaching the zone programmatically — Schedule Report, search, frequency select, status select, pause_circle / edit / delete row actions all reachable with a visible ring. The zone's contents are keyboard-operable; only the route into it is not (A11Y-3).
pause_circle / edit / delete icon buttons — icon-ligature text only, no aria-label; accessible name reads as the ligature ('pause_circle'). Dropped for the cap.

gaps: State map records no focus behaviour, no tab order and no accessible names anywhere — every finding here had to be established in a real browser, not from the map.
No screen reader was actually run (no NVDA/VoiceOver/Orca available). Accessible-name claims are computed from DOM semantics (labels, aria-*, text content), not from heard output.
Type cards are not focusable at all (tabIndex -1, programmatic .focus() fails), so Enter/Space activation of a report type could not be tested — only the absence of any keyboard route is proven.
Wizard step 3 (Run) was reached only by mouse/JS; its schedule toggle, frequency select and Run Now were not tab-walked, so the keyboard path through the final step is unverified.

The 'Edit a scheduled report' wizard and the Custom-period date inputs were not keyboard-interrogated; the state map lists the notify-by-email toggle as not_exercised and it stayed unexercised here too.
Focus behaviour of the six filter dropdown PANELS (containment, Escape, return to trigger) could not be tested, because the triggers cannot be opened from the keyboard in the first place.

findings.element: Type selection screen — the six report-type cards (.type-card: Punctuality DPM, Raw Data Export DPM, Data Quality Index (DQI) DPM, Connection Punctuality, Trip Failures DPM, Line Analysis DPM)
findings.finding: The six report-type cards are plain DIVs with an onclick handler, no role and no tabindex, so the screen that starts every evaluation has zero keyboard-focusable controls in its content area.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user can open 'New Evaluation' but can never choose a report type, so no evaluation can be created at all — the primary task dies on its first screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Make each card a real <button> (or add role="button" plus tabindex="0" and Enter/Space handlers) and give it an accessible name combining the type title and its one-line description.

evidence.action: Clicked 'New Evaluation', blurred the document, then pressed Tab 40 times and read document.activeElement after each press; also called .focus() directly on the first .type-card
evidence.observed: Only 11 stops exist and every one is page chrome — topbar nav ×5, lang select, Log out, and the four login utility buttons (Imprint/Documents/Support/Contact) — then focus wraps. Not one of the 6 visible .type-card elements is ever focused (any type-card focusable? false). Programmatic focus also fails: {focusedIsCard: false, tabIndex: -1}.

findings.element: Wizard step 2 (Filters) — all six filter triggers: #rpv-trigger, #mode-trigger, #canton-trigger, #tu-trigger, #lines-trigger, #stops-trigger
findings.finding: Every one of the six filter dropdowns is a DIV with no tabindex, no role, no aria-expanded and no aria-haspopup, so the entire Filters step is unreachable and un-announced by keyboard.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard-only user on the Filters step can only press Back or Next — they cannot set a single transport association, mode, canton, TU, line or stop, so the 'filters' half of period → filters → run is impossible and every evaluation they create runs unfiltered.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each trigger role="combobox" (or make it a <button>) with tabindex="0", aria-expanded reflecting the panel state and aria-haspopup="listbox", and wire Enter/Space/Arrow keys to open the panel and Escape to close it back onto the trigger.

evidence.action: Reached step 2, blurred the document, then pressed Tab 45 times reading document.activeElement each time; separately read tabindex/role/aria-expanded/aria-haspopup off all six .custom-select-trigger nodes
evidence.observed: The complete tab cycle is: topbar nav ×5 → lang select → Log out → Imprint/Documents/Support/Contact → button.btn-back 'Back' → button.btn 'Back' → button.btn 'Next' → wrap. No filter control ever receives focus. All six triggers report {tag: "div", tabindex: null, role: null, ariaExpanded: null, ariaHaspopup: null}.

findings.element: Left sidebar nav — div.nav-item 'Scheduled Reports' (and the same defect on 'Evaluations' and 'New Evaluation')
findings.finding: The only route to the Scheduled Reports screen is a DIV with onclick and no tabindex or role, so the whole scheduled-reports zone cannot be reached from the keyboard even though everything inside it is keyboard-operable.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard-only user can never open Scheduled Reports, so pausing, editing or deleting a scheduled evaluation — the 'manage scheduled evaluations' half of the primary task — is unreachable, not merely awkward.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the three sidebar nav-items real <button>s or <a href>s (or role="link" + tabindex="0" + Enter handling) inside a <nav>, with aria-current on the active one.

evidence.action: Blurred the document on the landing screen and pressed Tab until focus wrapped (53 presses, 18 unique stops), then queried every visible element whose text mentions 'Scheduled Reports' for focusability
evidence.observed: No div.nav-item appears anywhere in the 53-stop cycle (the stops are topbar ×5, lang, Log out, 4 util-links, New Evaluation, search, 2 filter selects, then only Anzeigen/delete row buttons). The single candidate route is {tag: "div", cls: "nav-item", tabindex: null, onclick: true, focusable: false}. Forcing the click via JS then reveals a fully tabbable zone (Schedule Report, search, 2 selects, pause/edit/delete), confirming the zone works and only the entrance is dead.

findings.element: Evaluations list — the 'delete' action icon on rows with status In Progress (button.action-icon.danger, pointer-events:none, opacity .35, title="Delete")
findings.finding: The delete button on In-Progress rows is disabled only visually — pointer-events:none and opacity .35, with no disabled attribute and no aria-disabled — so it stays in the tab order at tabIndex 0 and Enter really deletes the row.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user hears an ordinary enabled 'Delete' button and irreversibly deletes an in-progress evaluation that a mouse user is deliberately prevented from touching, with no warning that the action was meant to be unavailable.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the real disabled attribute (or aria-disabled="true" plus a guard in the click handler) on the In-Progress delete button and give it a name that states why, e.g. "Delete — unavailable while the evaluation is running".

evidence.action: Hit-tested the button with document.elementFromPoint, then focused it with .focus() and pressed Enter, accepting the native confirm()
evidence.observed: Mouse hit-test returns {hitIsButton: false, hitTag: "div.action-icons"} — the pointer cannot reach it. Keyboard focus lands on it fine (button.action-icon ["delete"], tabIndex 0, disabledAttr false, ariaDisabled null); Enter fires the native confirm 'Delete this evaluation? This action cannot be undone.' and on accept the row is gone: delete-buttons 34 → 33, 'In Progress' rows 6 → 5 (target row: 'Pünktlichkeit – Letzte 7 Tage, SBB · 19.05–25.05.2026 · In Progress'). Focus is then dumped on BODY.
